searchText: just published my initial work on a separate implementation of the `mev-boost` software to help out w/ Merge testing https://github.com/ralexstokes/mev-boost-rs expect things to be a little chaotic with the repo until we solidify the builder specs but if anyone is interested to help out w/ implementation let me know 🙂 can i run it on kiln network ? or how to easy setup the mev/builder infra for testing (and expect real payloads)? a docker-compose file would be most preferable is this with the EL or CL JSON? (and, is the point of that to be the first shared target, or are the links from https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/874767108809031740/969497410839670794 etc still current?) except for https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2884 being new I don't think this is specifying any boost setup as well : https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/wiki/Testing-infrastructure 🤔 well with the builder/relay API collapsed into the same thing a simple interim testing solution was supposed not to require mev-boost of any sort? just use mergemock directly for local testing? won't give any real payloads for kiln i suppose oh, right, yeah. An actual kiln setup would be useful anyone working in that direction? happy to coordinate (testing out the setup 😆 ) i think not and i haven’t tried. not sure the upstream to relay is fully implemented yet. and i’m focusing on the new CL-style API next EL JSON for now, will push CL style soon not sure the full builders specs are written yet yeah, I can't tell that either. The process has begun, but that's part of what I'm asking about interop test plans -- from a Nimbus perspective (and different CLs definitely differ here -- some are more modular in this regard), the EL-based JSON approach is just implemented differently enough from the CL-based one that if the latter [which I do think is better, per discussion previously] is a fait accompli, well, it doesn't make much sense to try to get a working/testable branch for the EL version. <@543900561460822016> ``` $ git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/lightclient/builder-apis Cloning into 'builder-apis'... remote: Enumerating objects: 77, done. remote: Counting objects: 100% (77/77), done. remote: Compressing objects: 100% (39/39), done. remote: Total 77 (delta 31), reused 72 (delta 26), pack-reused 0 Receiving objects: 100% (77/77), 21.39 KiB | 1.64 MiB/s, done. Resolving deltas: 100% (31/31), done. Submodule 'beacon-apis' (git@github.com:ethereum/beacon-APIs.git) registered for path 'beacon-apis' Cloning into '/home/user/builder-apis/beacon-apis'... git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey). fatal: Could not read from remote repository. ``` ? Maybe a local misconfiguration, Re testing: - for local testing, I'll implement the REST API spec into mergemock and mev-boost the coming days (should be ready middle of next week) - we'll get a proper builder and relay up and running for kiln the coming week, where clients can connect to and test with real payloads please prioritize kiln first if possible 🙏 would be cool to test it happening in real hm, at least having some sort of baseline sanity check ability is nice though but, yeah, obviously both are important Both will come next week! Development is already well underway and we're close. 🔥 hmm probably because i set the remote to be an ssh address i had the same issue, make sure your ssh key on github is registered w/ your local ssh agent (that fixed it for me) i can just set it to http for ease and re: specs, my understanding is that we are moving to this combo: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/209 and https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/2 now would be the time to review those PRs and chime in w/ any feedback, the sooner they get merged the sooner the rest of the testing infra can be developed so i implemented most of what is in `builder-specs#2` here https://github.com/ralexstokes/mev-boost-rs/pull/1 and found it is not quite complete yet but VERY close Here's a web-preview of the current builder REST API spec: https://builderspec-mevboost.metachris.com (i need to manually update, or <@543900561460822016> sets up cloudflare pages with read-access to his fork of the repo, then it can auto-build)
